investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-19T15:43–15:51Z with the identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the 6-node cluster had only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which were already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption victims were available, so the remote-agent pod remained unscheduled for 142 seconds before the eval timed out and returned no evidence. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity failure localized to the Swarm/kata-peerpods VM pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing remote agent provisioning (production-api environment) has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no node could accept a new remote-agent pod. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent was never created, and the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885: createAgent with machineType "remote") never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState — all four required evidence fields are missing (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence). The failure is localized to the kata-peerpods VM capacity layer, not to the eval runner logic or the expected-output contract definition.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on both eligible nodes: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource are fully allocated, leaving no capacity for a new remote-agent pod. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, concentrating all scheduling pressure on those 2 nodes and making capacity exhaustion more likely.

[Possible] Leaked or zombie remote-agent VMs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: a prior eval run or user session may have left VMs allocated without releasing them, consuming the available resource budget. No cleanup evidence is present in the packet to confirm or deny this.

[Possible but unconfirmed] Cluster autoscaler not configured or not triggered for kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes: if autoscaling is disabled or the node group has reached its maximum, new nodes cannot be added to absorb demand. No autoscaler signals are present in the supplied evidence.

[Low likelihood] Eval runner or createAgent logic error causing repeated pod submissions: the runner code at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885 appears straightforward; the scheduler message is a real infrastructure rejection, not a runner loop artifact.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity available (allocatable > used) on the eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the scheduler exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different cause (e.g., API-level rejection, auth failure, or runner bug) would need to be investigated.
If re-running the eval immediately after this failure produced a pass with all four required evidence fields present, it would suggest a transient spike rather than sustained exhaustion.

If the scheduler message were absent from the raw Kubernetes events and the eval failure message were generated by the runner itself (e.g., a timeout wrapper), the root cause would shift to the runner or API layer rather than the cluster scheduler.

If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state or remote-agent-runtime passed, the shared-dependency hypothesis would be weakened and the failure would be localized to the create path specifically.

If the node affinity/selector were changed to allow more nodes and the failure persisted, it would indicate the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes is the sole bottleneck rather than the affinity restriction.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that queries Kubernetes node capacity for kata.peerpods.io/vm (allocatable vs. used) and warns when headroom falls below a configurable threshold, providing early warning before pod scheduling fails.
Add a leaked-VM detection eval that lists all pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots older than a configurable TTL and fails if any are found in non-terminal states without an active agent session.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that counts how many cluster nodes satisfy the remote-agent pod's node selector/affinity and warns if fewer than a minimum number of nodes are eligible, catching configuration drift before it causes scheduling failures.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to capture and surface the Kubernetes scheduler rejection message as a structured evidence field (e.g., schedulerReason), so future failures include the cause in the evidence object rather than only in the check message.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-19T15:46–15:51Z with the identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes not matching pod affinity/selector. Because the pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a VM, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The production Kubernetes cluster's kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is exhausted on the two nodes that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector. Of the 6 available nodes, 4 do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints, and the remaining 2 have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those nodes. As a result, the eval runner's remote agent pod is stuck Unschedulable, the agent is never created, and all downstream state-polling and runtime checks fail with zero evidence collected. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

verifierContext.siblingCorrelation.likelySharedDependencyFailure: true — all three sibling checks share the same failure message, confirming a single upstream dependency (VM scheduling) is the common failure point.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota is fully consumed on the two affinity-matching nodes in the production cluster, leaving no schedulable capacity for new remote-agent pods. Preemption is not available because no lower-priority pods exist on those nodes.

[Secondary] The node affinity or selector configuration on the remote-agent pod template restricts scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes, concentrating VM resource pressure and making the cluster more susceptible to exhaustion under concurrent eval or user workloads.

[Less likely, no supporting evidence] A recent cluster scaling event or node failure reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a higher count to 2, shrinking available capacity without a corresponding quota adjustment.

[Least likely, no supporting evidence] The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource plugin or peer-pods controller on the two matching nodes is misconfigured or reporting a lower capacity than physically available.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-19T15:43–15:51Z with the identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the 6-node cluster had only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which were already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption victims were available, so the remote-agent pod remained unscheduled for 142 seconds before the eval timed out and returned no evidence. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity failure localized to the Swarm/kata-peerpods VM pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing remote agent provisioning (production-api environment) has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no node could accept a new remote-agent pod. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent was never created, and the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885: createAgent with machineType "remote") never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState — all four required evidence fields are missing (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence). The failure is localized to the kata-peerpods VM capacity layer, not to the eval runner logic or the expected-output contract definition.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on both eligible nodes: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource are fully allocated, leaving no capacity for a new remote-agent pod. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, concentrating all scheduling pressure on those 2 nodes and making capacity exhaustion more likely.

[Possible] Leaked or zombie remote-agent VMs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: a prior eval run or user session may have left VMs allocated without releasing them, consuming the available resource budget. No cleanup evidence is present in the packet to confirm or deny this.

[Possible but unconfirmed] Cluster autoscaler not configured or not triggered for kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes: if autoscaling is disabled or the node group has reached its maximum, new nodes cannot be added to absorb demand. No autoscaler signals are present in the supplied evidence.

[Low likelihood] Eval runner or createAgent logic error causing repeated pod submissions: the runner code at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885 appears straightforward; the scheduler message is a real infrastructure rejection, not a runner loop artifact.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity available (allocatable > used) on the eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the scheduler exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different cause (e.g., API-level rejection, auth failure, or runner bug) would need to be investigated.
If re-running the eval immediately after this failure produced a pass with all four required evidence fields present, it would suggest a transient spike rather than sustained exhaustion.

If the scheduler message were absent from the raw Kubernetes events and the eval failure message were generated by the runner itself (e.g., a timeout wrapper), the root cause would shift to the runner or API layer rather than the cluster scheduler.

If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state or remote-agent-runtime passed, the shared-dependency hypothesis would be weakened and the failure would be localized to the create path specifically.

If the node affinity/selector were changed to allow more nodes and the failure persisted, it would indicate the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes is the sole bottleneck rather than the affinity restriction.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that queries Kubernetes node capacity for kata.peerpods.io/vm (allocatable vs. used) and warns when headroom falls below a configurable threshold, providing early warning before pod scheduling fails.
Add a leaked-VM detection eval that lists all pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots older than a configurable TTL and fails if any are found in non-terminal states without an active agent session.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that counts how many cluster nodes satisfy the remote-agent pod's node selector/affinity and warns if fewer than a minimum number of nodes are eligible, catching configuration drift before it causes scheduling failures.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to capture and surface the Kubernetes scheduler rejection message as a structured evidence field (e.g., schedulerReason), so future failures include the cause in the evidence object rather than only in the check message.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-19T15:46–15:51Z with the identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes not matching pod affinity/selector. Because the pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a VM, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The production Kubernetes cluster's kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is exhausted on the two nodes that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector. Of the 6 available nodes, 4 do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints, and the remaining 2 have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those nodes. As a result, the eval runner's remote agent pod is stuck Unschedulable, the agent is never created, and all downstream state-polling and runtime checks fail with zero evidence collected. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the two affinity-matching nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm Allocatable > 0 and Requests = 0, the resource is not actually exhausted and the cause lies elsewhere (e.g., a misconfigured resource plugin or a stale scheduler cache).

If the remote-agent-state eval passes on a subsequent run without any cluster changes, the failure was transient (e.g., a briefly occupied slot was released) rather than a sustained capacity exhaustion.
If the scheduler message changes on re-run to reference a different error (e.g., image pull failure, quota exceeded at namespace level), the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion was not the root cause.

If sibling checks remote-agent-create and remote-agent-runtime pass while remote-agent-state continues to fail with a different message, the failure is isolated to the state-polling code path rather than shared VM scheduling.

If no remote-agent pods are found in a Pending/Unschedulable state in the cluster at the time of re-run, the scheduling layer is healthy and the failure may have been caused by a transient cluster event.
followUpEvals: Add an eval that directly checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on all nodes matching the remote-agent affinity/selector, alerting before the resource is fully exhausted rather than after pod scheduling fails.

Add an eval that monitors the count of Pending/Unschedulable remote-agent pods in the cluster and fires a warning when any pod has been unschedulable for more than a configurable threshold (e.g., 60s).

Add a pre-flight eval that verifies at least one node with sufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and matching affinity/selector exists before attempting remote agent creation, providing an earlier and more actionable failure signal.
Add a historical trend eval that tracks kata.peerpods.io/vm utilization over time to detect gradual capacity creep before it causes scheduling failures.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed with the identical Kubernetes scheduler message indicating zero schedulable nodes: 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, no agent was ever created, and the runtime eval received no evidence whatsoever — all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled (~142 s), preventing agent creation, state polling, and runtime chat from producing any evidence. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; this is an eval-layer failure reflecting the infrastructure state.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1918: 'const agent = await createAgent(args, track, "remote", null, orgId)' — the probe calls createAgent as its first substantive action; a scheduler failure here would abort all downstream evidence collection
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: the cluster has consumed all available peer-pod VM slots on the only nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving no schedulable capacity for new remote-agent pods.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, which may indicate a labeling change, node replacement, or taint addition that reduced the eligible node pool from a larger set to only 2 nodes, amplifying the impact of any VM slot exhaustion.

TERTIARY — Concurrent remote-agent workloads consuming all VM slots: other running pods may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources, leaving none available for the eval probe pods; preemption was explicitly reported as unable to help, suggesting no lower-priority victims exist.

UNLIKELY — Eval runner configuration issue: the runner correctly reached the scheduler (the scheduler message is explicit), so the failure is not a misconfigured token or missing org; the args.token guard at run-status-probes.mjs:1915 was passed.

reproductionSteps.details: Identify whether existing remote-agent pods or other workloads are holding all VM slots, and whether any are in a terminal or stuck state that could be cleaned up to free capacity.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agent pod scheduling — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool
affectedAreas.reason: The Kubernetes scheduler explicitly reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm on the 2 nodes eligible by affinity, blocking all remote-agent pod creation (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents feature — all three eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature (lines 183-185) failed with the same message, indicating the entire feature's eval surface is blocked by the shared scheduling dependency (evidence: source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189).

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — createAgent call for remote agent type
affectedAreas.reason: The runner branch at line 1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote'; this is the first point of failure when the scheduler cannot place the pod, causing all downstream evidence collection to be skipped (evidence: source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918).

affectedAreas.label: Node affinity/selector configuration for remote-agent pods
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto 2 nodes. If those rules have drifted or nodes have been relabeled, the eligible pool may be smaller than intended (evidence: failed-check.message).

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource utilization on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes in the production cluster to determine whether slots are fully consumed and by which pods.
Identify and terminate any stuck, leaked, or zombie remote-agent pods that may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without performing useful work, to free capacity for new scheduling attempts.

Assess whether the 4 nodes excluded by node affinity/selector rules should be eligible for remote-agent pods; if node labels have drifted or nodes were replaced without re-labeling, restore the correct labels to expand the schedulable pool.

Evaluate whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes is sufficient for the expected concurrent remote-agent eval and production workload; if not, plan node scaling or additional VM slot provisioning.
Re-run all three remote-agent eval checks after any capacity remediation to confirm recovery before closing the investigation.

Note that remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false (infra/evals/status/features.json line 185), so this check does not itself trigger an outage classification, but remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are required=true (lines 183-184) and their failure contributes to the degradedAfterFailures=1 threshold for the remote-agents feature.

A pass would indicate the capacity issue self-resolved; a repeat fail with the same message confirms sustained exhaustion (evidence: verifierContext.recommendedVerifierProbes, reproductionHint).

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly proves or disproves VM slot exhaustion as the root cause. If allocatable minus used equals zero, exhaustion is confirmed.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Run cluster node inspection tooling against the nodes that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector to read current kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity figures.

recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Query the cluster for all pods with kata.peerpods.io/vm resource requests in the production namespace to identify whether stuck, leaked, or long-running remote-agent pods are consuming all available slots.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run all three remote-agent sibling checks together to confirm shared dependency
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: If all three fail with the identical scheduler message again, the shared upstream dependency hypothesis is confirmed. If one passes, the failure is not purely a cluster-wide capacity issue.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect node labels and taints on all 6 nodes to validate affinity/selector scope
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Rules out a node configuration drift as a contributing factor that amplified the impact of any VM slot exhaustion.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Check whether the 4 nodes excluded by affinity rules were recently relabeled, tainted, or replaced, which would have reduced the eligible scheduling pool from a potentially larger set.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 affinity-matching nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity still available (i.e., slots are not exhausted), the root cause is not VM resource exhaustion and another scheduler constraint must be investigated.

If a fresh eval run succeeds immediately without any cluster changes, the failure was transient (e.g., a burst of concurrent workloads that have since completed) rather than a sustained capacity ceiling.

If the 4 non-matching nodes are found to have kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and the affinity rules are confirmed correct, the diagnosis shifts to a node labeling or taint regression that reduced the eligible pool.

If no pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm resources on the 2 eligible nodes despite the scheduler reporting exhaustion, a resource quota object or LimitRange at the namespace level may be the actual constraint rather than per-node capacity.

If the remote-agent-create sibling check passes in isolation while remote-agent-runtime fails, the failure is not a shared scheduling dependency and the diagnosis of shared upstream failure would need revision.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that directly checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on affinity-eligible nodes before attempting agent creation, so scheduling exhaustion is surfaced as a distinct infrastructure capacity signal rather than a timeout.
Add an eval that counts the number of currently running remote-agent pods and alerts when the count approaches the kata.peerpods.io/vm slot ceiling, providing early warning before full exhaustion.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector rules meets a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 2 nodes), catching pool shrinkage from relabeling or node loss.

Consider a canary eval that attempts remote-agent pod scheduling with a dry-run or low-priority pod to detect scheduling feasibility without consuming a VM slot, enabling faster detection of capacity constraints.
